1.say: Cross the short blue tail over the front of the long blue standing part. Hold the crossing and leave a round open loop hanging below.
placements: blue rope tail → across front of blue standing part at center crossing, forming one open round loop hanging below; in the video: tail points left, loop hangs lower-right
watch_for: If the tail goes under instead of over, you will not get the open loop - the tail must lie across the front.
If the loop is tiny or twisted closed, you left too little rope - the loop should hang open and round below the crossing.
1.check_yourself: The blue rope forms one open loop with the tail lying across the front of the standing part.

2.say: Bring the blue tail behind the blue standing part and around to the side. Keep the lower blue loop open below.
placements: blue rope tail → behind and around blue standing part to stick out sideways from behind the twist, above the open lower loop; in the video: tail sticks out to the right, loop hangs to lower-left
watch_for: If the tail stays in front of the standing part, it did not go behind - the tail must disappear behind the standing part at the twist.
If the lower loop collapses closed, you pulled too far - keep the lower loop open and round.
2.check_yourself: The blue rope shows an upper twist around the standing part with the tail sticking out sideways behind it and the lower loop still open.

3.say: Feed the blue tail down through the center of the lower blue loop. Pull the long top end and the short bottom tail opposite to tighten.
placements: blue rope short tail → down through center of lower blue loop and pulled straight down below knot to tighten; in the video: exits centered below two stacked loops
watch_for: If you get an overhand instead of an 8, the tail went through the wrong opening - it must go down through the lower open loop.
If the knot looks loose or crooked, it is not dressed - pull both ends firmly until the two loops stack neatly.
3.check_yourself: The blue rope forms a tight figure-eight with two stacked loops and the tail exiting straight below.
